title: Halting after a deterministic instruction
statement: Let $A$ be a nondeterministic register program, with fixed oracle, input, and configuration predicate $G$. Suppose the instruction at state $l$ is the deterministic instruction $i$, and let $\beta$ be either Boolean value. If $(l,v,r)$ satisfies $G$, and every choice word of length $N$ from the configuration obtained by applying $i$ at $(l,v,r)$ leads to a halted configuration while all its earlier nonhalted configurations satisfy $G$, then every choice word of length $N+1$ from $(l,v,r)$ has those same halting and intermediate-configuration properties.
hypotheses_covered: A nondeterministic register program $A$, oracle, input, and predicate $G$
State $l$ and deterministic instruction $i$, with the instruction at $l$ equal to $i$
A register valuation $v$, result value $r$, and natural number $N$
The length-$N$ halting and intermediate-$G$ property holds from the configuration obtained by the deterministic step using $\beta$
